* Jetpacs ↔ Material 3 Component Reference

This document maps every user-facing Material Design 3 composable (from
=material3= *1.4.0*) to its Jetpacs wire type and Elisp DSL function, showing
which M3 components Jetpacs already wraps and which are available for future
expansion.

*Version provenance:* =material3= carries NO pinned version — it resolves
through the Compose BOM (=compose-bom = "2026.02.01"= in
=libs.versions.toml=), which constrains it to *1.4.0* (verified
2026-07-28 via =dependencyInsight=; see the generator section).  When the
BOM moves, re-verify and regenerate — the unwrapped list changes with the
version (=FloatingToolbar= and =SplitButton= arrive in 1.5+).

| Metric | Count |
|---+---|
| ✅ M3 components wrapped by Jetpacs | 30 |
| ≈ M3 components approximated (contract met, composable unused) | 1 |
| ⬜ M3 components available (unwrapped) | 14 |
| Infrastructure classes (excluded) | 27 |

** How to Read This Table

- *✅ Wrapped*: Jetpacs exposes this M3 component through its wire format.
  Use the =Wire Type= and =Elisp Function= columns to access it.
- *≈ Approximated*: the wire slot and the CHROME-VOCABULARY contract
  exist, but the renderer builds the visuals from generic composables
  instead of invoking the real M3 component — fidelity gaps (insets,
  scroll behaviors, indicator pills) are hand-managed or absent.
- *⬜ Available*: This M3 component exists in the library but Jetpacs does
  not yet wrap it.  It could be added by defining a new wire type,
  Elisp constructor, and renderer case.

** Generating This Table

The component list comes from the RESOLVED =material3= AAR — never from
"the first AAR in the Gradle cache", which holds every version ever
resolved.  Two steps, portable (python3 + a populated cache):

1. Confirm the resolved version (material3 rides the Compose BOM):

#+begin_src sh :results output
cd ../../companion && ./gradlew -q :app:dependencyInsight \
  --dependency androidx.compose.material3:material3 \
  --configuration debugCompileClasspath | head -1
#+end_src

2. Regenerate the raw list for that version and record it in the header:

#+begin_src sh :results output
python3 generate-component-list.py 1.4.0
#+end_src

The Status / Wire Type / Elisp Function / Notes columns of the
cross-reference are maintained BY HAND — diff the regenerated raw list
against the table's =M3 Component= column and reconcile additions and
removals.

** Unwrapped Components — Expansion Opportunities

These M3 components are available in the library but not yet exposed through
the Jetpacs wire format.  Each represents a potential new wire type.

*** BottomSheetScaffold / ModalBottomSheet

Persistent or modal bottom sheets.  Could expose as a =bottom_sheet= wire
type with child content, or integrate into =scaffold= as a =bottom_sheet=
property.

*Precedent:* The =scaffold= already hosts =drawer=, =snackbar=, and =fab=
as optional children — a bottom sheet would fit naturally here.

*** Carousel

A horizontally scrolling card carousel (=material3.carousel=).  Could map
to a =carousel= wire type with =items= children, similar to =tabs= but
optimized for card-sized content.

*** DateRangePicker

Extends =date_button= with a start/end date range.  Could be a
=date_range_button= wire type returning ={start, end}= ISO dates.

*** ExposedDropdownMenu

A dropdown menu anchored to a text field.  Partially covered by =enum_list=
(which uses =FlowRow= + =FilterChip=), but this provides the classic
dropdown UX.  Could be a =dropdown= wire type.

*** Label

A tooltip-style label that points to an anchor.  Useful for onboarding
flows.  Could be a =label= universal attribute rather than a node type.

*** ListItem

A structured list row with headline, supporting text, leading/trailing
content.  Jetpacs currently achieves this with manual =row=/=column=
composition inside =card=.  A dedicated =list_item= wire type would
reduce boilerplate.

*** NavigationBar

Bottom navigation bar.  Would complement =scaffold= — could be the
=bottom_bar= renderer when children are navigation items rather than
arbitrary nodes.

*** NavigationRail

Side navigation rail for larger screens.  Similar to =NavigationBar= but
vertical.  Relevant for tablet/foldable layouts.

*** RadioButton

Exclusive-choice radio buttons.  Currently achievable via =enum_list=
with =multi_select: false=, but a dedicated =radio_group= wire type
would be more semantic.

*** SearchBar

An expanding search bar with suggestions.  Could be a =search_bar= wire
type with =on_query_change= and =suggestions= children.

*** SecureTextField

A text field with obfuscation (for passwords/PINs).  Partially available
via =text_input :password t= which uses =OutlinedTextField= with
=visualTransformation=.

*** SegmentedButton

A single-row button group for selecting between 2–5 options.  Semantically
similar to =tabs= but with a different visual treatment (no pager).  Could
be a =segmented_button= wire type.

*** TextField (filled variant)

Jetpacs uses =OutlinedTextField= exclusively.  The filled variant is
available but intentionally not exposed — outlined is the canonical M3
text field style.

** Infrastructure Classes (Excluded)

The following classes from the =material3= package are infrastructure,
theming tokens, state holders, or internal utilities — not user-facing
composable components:

- =AppBarColumn=, =AppBarDsl=, =AppBarRow= — internal AppBar layout helpers
- =CarouselState=, =WideNavigationRailState= — state holders
- =ContentColor= — =LocalContentColor= composition local
- =DateInput=, =DateRangeInput= — internal date field renderers
- =DatePickerDialog=, =TimePickerDialog= — dialog wrappers (used internally)
- =DragHandle= — bottom sheet drag affordance
- =DynamicTonalPalette=, =TonalPalette= — color generation utilities
- =HorizontalCenterOptically= — layout modifier
- =InteractiveComponentSize= — minimum touch target sizing
- =KeylineList=, =Keylines=, =KeylineSnapPosition=, =Strategy= — carousel internals
- =MotionScheme= — animation token scheme
- =NavigationItem= — internal item for NavigationBar/Rail
- =Ripple= — touch feedback indicator
- =SecureTextField= — password field (text_input :password covers this)
- =Shapes= — shape token scheme
- =SheetDefaults= — bottom sheet configuration defaults
- =ShortNavigationBar=, =WideNavigationRail= — adaptive navigation variants

** Notes

- *Version lock:* This table reflects =material3= *1.4.0*. Newer versions
  may add components (e.g., =SplitButton=, =FloatingToolbar= in 1.5+).
  Regenerate after updating the dependency.
- *Jetpacs wire types are not 1:1 with M3 components.* A single wire type
  like =scaffold= uses 8+ M3 composables internally; a single M3 component
  like =OutlinedTextField= serves 2 wire types (=text_input= and =editor=).
- *The spec governs expansion.* Adding a new M3 component to Jetpacs
  requires: (1) a new wire type in =ebp/contract.json= =node_schema=,
  (2) an Elisp constructor in =jetpacs-widgets.el=, (3) a renderer case
  in the companion, (4) registration in =NodeSupport.kt=, and (5) golden
  test coverage.
